Class RowGroupWriter

Namespace
ParquetNeo
Assembly
ParquetNeo.dll

Writes one row group: every column of the schema, in schema order, each with the same number of rows. Create it with AppendRowGroup(), call NextColumn() once per column, and dispose it (or call Close()) to finish the group.

Dispose()

Finishes the group if every column was written. Problems (a missing column, a column without values, mismatched row counts) are not reported from here, so that disposing never hides an exception that is already on its way: the file is abandoned instead and Close() then fails. Call Close() to get the error at the point where it happens.

WriteColumns(IReadOnlyList<Action<ColumnWriter>>, int, CancellationToken)

Writes every column of the group, encoding up to maxDegreeOfParallelism of them at a time. Encoding (the dictionary, the levels, compression, statistics) is most of the time of writing, so a group of several columns takes about as long as its slowest column instead of the sum of them.

public void WriteColumns(IReadOnlyList<Action<ColumnWriter>> columns, int maxDegreeOfParallelism, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)

Parameters

columns IReadOnlyList<Action<ColumnWriter>>

What to write to each column, in the order of the schema.

maxDegreeOfParallelism int

The most columns encoded at the same time; at least 1.

cancellationToken CancellationToken

Stops the columns that have not started; the exception is an OperationCanceledException.

Remarks

The columns are encoded into buffers of their own, and then copied to the file in the order of the schema, so the file is the same, byte for byte, as the one NextColumn() makes whatever the degree of parallelism. The group must not have started: this does all of its columns.

The actions run on different threads, one thread for each action, so they must not share anything that is not safe to share (the arrays they read from are fine as long as nothing writes to them). The ColumnWriter an action gets is for that action alone and only until it returns: write the values of the column to it and do not keep it. The action does not complete the column; the group does.

The encoded columns of the group are held in memory until all of them are done, so this takes about the size of the group (compressed) more memory than NextColumn(), which writes each column to the file as it goes. If an action throws, that exception is thrown from here, nothing of the group is written, and disposing the group abandons the file. Use NextColumn() for a group that is too big to hold, or for a single column.

WriteColumns(IReadOnlyList<Action<ColumnWriter>>, CancellationToken)

Writes every column of the group on as many threads as the machine has processors; see WriteColumns(IReadOnlyList<Action<ColumnWriter>>, int, CancellationToken).
